question: What is Schwab's strategy for its RIA custody business?

claims.text: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) describes Advisor Services as providing custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent RIAs, independent retirement advisors and recordkeepers. It says management has adopted a firm-wide strategy described as "Through Clients' Eyes."

The 2025 10-K states that management believes Schwab can maintain its competitive position in Advisor Services primarily through sales, support, technology and business consulting teams "dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed." The filing also says Schwab uses technology to provide RIAs with a "highly-developed, scalable platform."

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab is deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone. He cited lending support, alternatives capability, an institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform with funds from nearly 60 managers, and the Advisor ProDirect launch for breakaway advisors.

On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), Wurster named three Advisor Services monetization areas: wealth (Model Market Center and alternative investments), expanding lending and trust services to advisors through Charles Schwab Bank, and "industry-leading trading capabilities," including a high-touch block-trade service planned for Q1. He also said Schwab is "winning on all fronts in Advisor Services" and that the business grew about 6.5% organically last year.

On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), Wurster said Schwab is continuing to enhance digital experiences across RIA workflows such as move money, account open and account maintenance, while modernizing tools on its adviser platform.

On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), Wurster said Schwab has continued to expand its branch footprint and hire financial consultants, wealth advisers and relationship managers for RIA clients while advancing AI capabilities.

On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Wurster said Schwab built its adviser business around "helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed." He described a platform bringing together custody, trading, banking and lending, technology and dedicated service. He said more than 1,100 advisory firms added Schwab as a custodian last year, "more than 3x the number of the next closest provider," and that Schwab is continuing to invest in the business. He also said Schwab is the first RIA custodian included in Anthropic's Claude for Financial Advisors.

Trade press (WealthManagement.com, 2026-10-29; indicative only) reports that Wurster said Schwab wants RIAs to have equal or better access than wirehouse counterparts to lending, private market investing and long-short strategies. It quotes him saying Schwab is "increasingly trying to play a role of being their bank." Separate trade press (2026-10-28) reports he committed to keep serving RIAs with under $100 million in client assets.

The 2025 10-K names the competition in the Advisor Services arena as institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks and trust companies. The 10-K also says price competition (for example reduced commissions, higher deposit rates or lower expense ratios) could affect results.

Trade press (WealthManagement.com, 2026-08-26; indicative only) reports that Vanguard's $4.6 billion outlay for Altruist makes it a more formidable RIA-custody competitor. It quotes Datos Insights' Will Trout saying that "Both have absorbed real share loss to Altruist already," and that Schwab and Fidelity still have a commanding lead. This is an analyst view, not a Schwab statement.

Pulling back on referrals: trade press (InvestmentNews, 2026-08-24; indicative only) reports that a Schwab spokesperson confirmed the Schwab Advisor Network referral minimum rises from $2 million to $5 million effective Jan. 5, 2027. It follows an earlier rise from $500,000 to $2 million. Trade press (2026-10-15) adds that the AUM threshold for firms entering SAN rose to at least $500 million from $250 million. The 2026-10-28 article quotes Wurster saying SAN has 100 participating firms out of the 17,000 custodying with Schwab and that Schwab will continue to invest in SAN. A recruiter and consultants quoted in these articles say RIAs are losing a referral source and may look to other custodians.

Pulling back on long/short: trade press (2026-10-28; indicative only) reports that Schwab limited long-short tax strategies to clients with at least $10 million in assets after they were quickly oversubscribed. It reports Wurster saying Schwab is working with third-party providers and developing a proprietary offering. On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Wurster said the long/short program helped drive some NNA, that Schwab changed the minimums and "throttled growth to some extent," and that Advisor Services NNA growth "has in no way slowed at all."

Competing for client relationships: trade press (RIABiz, 2026-08-20; indicative only) reports that Schwab is hiring "thousands more financial consultants" and steering sub-$5-million investors away from RIAs. An RIA CEO quoted by InvestmentNews (2026-08-24) says this could hurt Schwab's RIA custodial business. Management's own framing on the 1Q26 call (April 2026) was that as independent advisers win, "we win as well."

Trade press (WealthManagement.com, 2026-10-28; indicative only) reports that Fidelity told RIAs in early October that firms with under $100 million in client assets must leave its platform by June 30, 2027. It says Schwab and other custodians are seeking to capitalize on this.

Advisor Services client assets were $5,845.9 billion at 3Q26 (September 30, 2026), per the earnings release dated 2026-10-15. The release's percent-change columns show 17% and 2%. The same table shows 3Q26 Advisor Services net new assets of $120.1 billion, with percent-change columns of 47% and 50%, against $80.2 billion in the next column.

Earlier quarterly Advisor Services net new assets in the releases: $80.2 billion in 2Q26 (release 2026-07-21), $85.8 billion in 1Q26 (release 2026-04-16), and $97.8 billion in 4Q25 (release 2026-01-21).
Schwab's August 2026 monthly activity report (published 2026-09-15) shows Advisor Services assets receiving ongoing advisory services of 5,903.0 (billions), up 21% year over year.

Management reports Advisor Services metrics and rankings. The 2Q26 deck (2026-07-21) and 3Q26 transcript (2026-10-15) rank Schwab #1 in RIA custodial assets. On the 3Q26 call, Wurster said more than 16,000 firms represent $5.8 trillion, and more than 1,100 firms added Schwab as custodian last year. The 3Q26 deck shows a transfer-of-assets (TOA) ratio of approximately 1.8x; the call transcript describes this as firm-wide. On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), Wurster said Advisor Services NNA and TOA were "both accelerating."

Trade press (WealthManagement.com, 2026-10-15; indicative only) reports that Schwab said it added 1,001 new RIAs to its custody platform in Q3, versus 349, 339, 202 and 79 for its nearest unnamed peers. It also reports that 36% of joiners had AUM above $5 billion and 13% had $1 billion to $5 billion.

Trade press (RIABiz, 2026-09-23; indicative only) reports specific breakaway wins custodying at Schwab, including Rise Private Wealth Management, which it says is near $8 billion in assets, and StackStone Wealth at $1.9 billion in assets administered.

The 2025 10-K describes the RIA technology platform: the Advisor Services website for account opening, money movement, transfers and trading; third-party integrations; Schwab Advisor Portfolio Connect, available free of charge to advisors; the thinkpipes trading platform; and iRebal for rebalancing. It also describes consulting services, transition support and the Advisor ProDirect membership program launched in 2025.

Pricing and economics: the 2025 10-K says that as custodian, Schwab earns revenue on the underlying client assets, predominantly through net interest revenue and asset management and administration fees. It states that Schwab does not charge the RIA or end client a custody fee. The 10-K also says net revenues in both segments come from client assets and trading activity, with differences based on asset composition, trading frequency and pricing unique to each segment.

Banking and lending: on the 2Q26 call (July 2026), Wurster said RIAs value the bank because they do not have to introduce another relationship to their clients. He said lending balances rose 33% year over year, driven in large part by the digital Pledged Asset Line, and that Schwab is adding structured asset lending. The 2Q26 release (2026-07-21) said long/short strategy interest stayed strong among RIA clients, with margin loan debits of $42.1 billion and short cash credits of $43.7 billion as of June 30, 2026.

Technology and AI (trade press, indicative only): reports from late October and early November 2026 say Schwab made Claude for Financial Advisors available in the Advisor Center, limited to read-only access. It is offering a $4,800 credit for the enterprise version for sign-ups by Nov. 30. Schwab took a minority stake in Nevis, a back-office AI platform, which is to go live for advisors in Q1 2027 and which RIAs pay for separately. The Wealth.com tax and estate tool is free until February 2027 and fee-based afterwards. Schwab now requires Docusign for agreements. Syntax Direct integrates with iRebal. Beatty said a business banking checking account is coming next year.

The 2026 investor-day deck (published 2026-05-14) lists planned Advisor Services expansion items: AI-enabled tax planning, Structured Asset Line, wealth specializations, UHNW experiences and digital banking enhancements for RIAs. It describes "the leading RIA support ecosystem" providing wealth tools, investment and lending products and technology in addition to custody and service.

adjacent.text: On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), CFO Mike Verdeschi said total cash levels run around 10% of client assets, with transactional cash at about 4%, or approximately $10,000 per account. He said independent RIAs continue to help their end clients manage portfolio allocations, including cash.
adjacent.differs_because: These cash figures are given for the firm overall, not for Advisor Services, and they do not describe bank sweep economics or pricing for RIA custody.

gaps.what: Advisor Services-specific bank sweep and cash economics (sweep rates, cash yield, net interest revenue on RIA assets) are not found in the evidence provided. Only the firm-wide cash allocation is given.
gaps.suggested_source: Schwab 10-K/10-Q Advisor Services segment tables and net interest revenue disclosures; earnings-call Q&A on cash

gaps.what: Advisor Services segment revenue, margin and any RIA-specific pricing schedule are not found in the evidence provided (the segment table was truncated).
gaps.suggested_source: Schwab 10-K Item 7 and Note 24 segment information

gaps.what: Official Schwab disclosure of RIA attrition, or of Schwab custody share loss to named competitors (for example Altruist), is not found. The share-loss claim comes only from a trade-press analyst quote.
gaps.suggested_source: Schwab Fall/Investor Day business-update materials or custodian market-share studies
